title: Synesis for IRaMuTeQ Users
text:
This tutorial is for researchers who already know IRaMuTeQ and want to understand how the Synesis language can complement — and extend — their qualitative analysis workflow.
You will learn to:

Structure a corpus directly in Synesis, from data collection on
Create a typed template with automatic validation
Generate the IRaMuTeQ corpus from the Synesis project
Add annotation layers that feed analyses beyond IRaMuTeQ

Prerequisite: familiarity with the IRaMuTeQ corpus format (**** lines, variables and modalities).



The traditional workflow starts outside the software: the researcher prepares a .txt file with **** lines, usually in a text editor, and loads it for analysis. Nothing validates the research design: a non-existent modality or a missing field produces silent noise in the results.
For small corpora and solo researchers this is manageable. For hundreds of texts, several coders or distinct collection phases, it becomes a real methodological risk.
Synesis inverts the flow: the corpus is kept in Synesis from the start, validated by the compiler at every edit, and converted to IRaMuTeQ on demand. The IRaMuTeQ .txt becomes a derived artifact, generated from the canonical source.




IRaMuTeQ organizes the corpus with command lines preceding each text. Each line starts with **** and lists variables in the form *name_value.


This corpus gathers answers to the question “What do you think about Aids?”, collected from secondary school students (Antunes, 2012). It is one of the canonical examples for Descending Hierarchical Classification (DHC) with short answers. The texts are in Portuguese, as in the original.






IRaMuTeQ Tutorial



The examples in this tutorial come from the IRaMuTeQ user manual (Camargo & Justo, 2021).
The case-study repository holds the ready-to-use project.










Variable
Description
IRaMuTeQ modalities




*ind
Participant
001 to 312


*sex
Sex
1 = male, 2 = female


*sch
Type of school
1 = public, 2 = private


*kno
Knows someone HIV-positive
1 = yes, 2 = no


*tra
Knowledge about transmission
1 = good, 2 = little


*att
Attitude towards HIV-positive people
1 = favorable, 2 = neutral, 3 = unfavorable



**** *ind_001 *sex_1 *sch_2 *kno_2 *tra_1 *att_3
A aids é um vírus que tem que tomar muito cuidado. É importante conhecer
seu parceiro na hora de realizar atos sexuais. O vírus pode ser transmitido
por causa de um ato irresponsável, transar sem o uso de um preservativo,
ou através de um estupro.
**** *ind_002 *sex_2 *sch_2 *kno_1 *tra_2 *att_1
Aids: quando citado, me vem na cabeça a quantidade de pessoas que possuem
o vírus e que sofrem preconceito diante disto, por terem a doença.
Each **** block is an initial context unit: the values after **** are the respondent’s metadata and the following text is the analysed content.





The template (.synt) declares the fields, their types and their rules. In Synesis the modalities have readable names; the numeric IRaMuTeQ code is applied only on export.

TEMPLATE aids_corpus version: "1.0"

# ============================================
# SOURCE FIELDS
# ============================================

SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED ind, sex, sch, kno, tra, att
END SOURCE FIELDS

FIELD ind TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Unique participant identifier
END FIELD

FIELD sex TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Sex of the participant
    VALUES
        Male: Male
        Female: Female
    END VALUES
END FIELD

FIELD sch TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Type of school attended
    VALUES
        Public: Public school
        Private: Private school
    END VALUES
END FIELD

FIELD kno TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Knows someone HIV-positive
    VALUES
        Knows: Knows at least one HIV-positive person
        Does_not_know: Knows no HIV-positive person
    END VALUES
END FIELD

FIELD tra TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Knowledge about HIV transmission
    VALUES
        Good: Good knowledge
        Little: Little knowledge
    END VALUES
END FIELD

FIELD att TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Attitude towards HIV-positive people
    VALUES
        Favorable: Favorable attitude
        Neutral: Neutral attitude
        Unfavorable: Unfavorable attitude
    END VALUES
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ITEM FIELDS
# ============================================

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED answer
    OPTIONAL chain
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD answer TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Answer to the open question about Aids
    GUIDELINES
        Copy the whole answer, without correcting spelling.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    DESCRIPTION Relation between ideas stated in the answer
    RELATIONS
        INHIBITS: one concept reduces or blocks another
        PROMOTES: one concept favors or expands another
        ASSOCIATES: association between concepts
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ONTOLOGY FIELDS
# ============================================

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED definition
    OPTIONAL group
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Definition of the concept in the context of representations of Aids
END FIELD

FIELD group TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Thematic grouping of the concept
END FIELD
Why it matters: an attempt to record att: Neutro or sex: Other is rejected by the compiler before the datum reaches IRaMuTeQ, with a suggestion of the closest value.




Each respondent is a SOURCE + ITEM pair. File aids_corpus.syn:

SOURCE @ind_001
    ind: 001
    sex: Male
    sch: Private
    kno: Does_not_know
    tra: Good
    att: Unfavorable
END SOURCE

ITEM @ind_001
    answer: "A aids é um vírus que tem que tomar muito cuidado. É importante conhecer seu parceiro na hora de realizar atos sexuais."
END ITEM

SOURCE @ind_002
    ind: 002
    sex: Female
    sch: Private
    kno: Knows
    tra: Little
    att: Favorable
END SOURCE

ITEM @ind_002
    answer: "Aids: quando citado, me vem na cabeça a quantidade de pessoas que possuem o vírus e que sofrem preconceito diante disto, por terem a doença."
    chain: social_prejudice -> INHIBITS -> family_support
END ITEM

SOURCE @ind_003
    ind: 003
    sex: Female
    sch: Private
    kno: Does_not_know
    tra: Little
    att: Unfavorable
END SOURCE

ITEM @ind_003
    answer: "Eu penso que é uma questão complicada, porque a pessoa fica mal e tem que viver de remédios e tem medo de passar pra outra."
END ITEM
The ontology (aids_corpus.syno) defines the concepts used in chains:

ONTOLOGY social_prejudice
    definition: Rejection of or discrimination against HIV-positive people
    group: social_dimension
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY family_support
    definition: Help from relatives and friends to people living with HIV/Aids
    group: social_dimension
END ONTOLOGY
The bibliography (aids_corpus.bib) has one entry per respondent, with a neutral key:

@misc{ind_001, author = {Participant 001}, title = {Answer 001}, year = {2012}}
@misc{ind_002, author = {Participant 002}, title = {Answer 002}, year = {2012}}
@misc{ind_003, author = {Participant 003}, title = {Answer 003}, year = {2012}}
And the project (aids_corpus.synp):

PROJECT aids_corpus
    TEMPLATE "aids_corpus.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "aids_corpus.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "aids_corpus.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "aids_corpus.syno"
END PROJECT



Example project in the Synesis extension.






The compiler has no IRaMuTeQ exporter. The conversion is a short step over the compiled JSON. First:
synesis compile aids_corpus.synp --json corpus.json
Then save this script as to_iramuteq.py:

import json
import re

# Numeric code IRaMuTeQ will receive for each modality
CODES = {
    "sex": {"Male": "1", "Female": "2"},
    "sch": {"Public": "1", "Private": "2"},
    "kno": {"Knows": "1", "Does_not_know": "2"},
    "tra": {"Good": "1", "Little": "2"},
    "att": {"Favorable": "1", "Neutral": "2", "Unfavorable": "3"},
}
VARIABLES = ["ind", "sex", "sch", "kno", "tra", "att"]
TEXT_FIELD = "answer"

with open("corpus.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

lines = []
for item in data["corpus"]:
    key = item["source_ref"].lstrip("@")
    source = data["bibliography"][key]        # includes the SOURCE fields
    marks = []
    for var in VARIABLES:
        value = str(source[var])
        if var == "ind":
            value = value.zfill(3)            # 001 is read as the number 1
        marks.append(f"*{var}_{CODES.get(var, {}).get(value, value)}")
    text = item["data"][TEXT_FIELD].strip().strip('"')
    text = re.sub(r"[*$%\"]", " ", text)      # characters IRaMuTeQ reserves
    lines.append("**** " + " ".join(marks))
    lines.append(text)

with open("aids_iramuteq.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

print(f"{len(data['corpus'])} texts written to aids_iramuteq.txt")
python to_iramuteq.py
The generated file opens in IRaMuTeQ (UTF-8 encoding):
**** *ind_001 *sex_1 *sch_2 *kno_2 *tra_1 *att_3
A aids é um vírus que tem que tomar muito cuidado. É importante conhecer seu parceiro na hora de realizar atos sexuais.
**** *ind_002 *sex_2 *sch_2 *kno_1 *tra_2 *att_1
Aids: quando citado, me vem na cabeça a quantidade de pessoas que possuem o vírus e que sofrem preconceito diante disto, por terem a doença.



Synesis
IRaMuTeQ




SOURCE block
variables of the **** line


Field sex: Male
*sex_1


Field att: Unfavorable
*att_3


QUOTATION field of the ITEM
text following the **** line



Adapt CODES, VARIABLES and TEXT_FIELD to your template. From there on, DHC, similarity analysis, correspondence analysis and word clouds proceed as usual, with the guarantee that the corpus was validated first.




The main advantage of keeping the corpus in Synesis is that one source feeds several destinations:
Synesis corpus (.synp + .bib + .syn + .synt + .syno)
        │
        ├──► the compiler validates against the template
        │       └── errors reported before analysis
        │
        ├──► JSON ──► script ──► IRaMuTeQ (.txt)
        │                         └── DHC, similarity, CA, word cloud
        │
        ├──► CSV / Excel ──► spreadsheets, R, pandas
        │
        ├──► synesis.load() in Jupyter
        │         ├── sources     → SOURCE variables
        │         ├── items       → texts and ITEM fields
        │         ├── ontologies  → concepts
        │         └── chains      → relations
        │
        ├──► synesis-graph ──► graph (HTML, Neo4j, ArcadeDB)
        │
        └──► further coding in the corpus itself
                ├── CODE, CHAIN   (categories and relations)
                ├── MEMO          (analytical notes)
                └── SCALE         (scores per item)


After running the DHC and identifying thematic classes, return to the corpus and enrich it. For instance, add an ENUMERATED field to the template for the DHC class, or record a relation:
ITEM @ind_002
    answer: "Quando citado, me vem na cabeça a quantidade de pessoas que sofrem preconceito."
    chain: social_prejudice -> INHIBITS -> family_support
END ITEM
These annotations do not change the IRaMuTeQ .txt, but they are available to the graph, to the tables and to a second IRaMuTeQ round with variables derived from the coding.



import synesis

project = synesis.SynesisCompiler("aids_corpus.synp").compile()
project.to_csv("tables/")      # sources.csv, items.csv, chains.csv...
To work entirely in memory, with DataFrames, use synesis.load.





For solo researchers with small corpora, IRaMuTeQ alone is enough. Synesis makes a difference in three scenarios:
Large corpora. With hundreds of participants, typos in variables are likely. The compiler catches them before analysis.
Team work. The template works as a contract: fields, allowed values and relations live in one versionable file. Divergences show at compile time.
Longitudinal research. As the corpus grows, the template keeps integrity across versions, and conceptual decisions can be documented in the .syno:
# DECISION 2026-03-01: we split "prejudice" into two concepts after
# telling declared prejudice apart from reported behaviour.

ONTOLOGY declared_prejudice
    definition: Verbal expression of a discriminatory attitude
    group: social_dimension
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY behavioural_prejudice
    definition: Discriminatory action reported by the participant
    group: social_dimension
END ONTOLOGY












Aspect
IRaMuTeQ
Synesis + IRaMuTeQ




Corpus validation
File format
Fields and modalities of the design


Canonical source
.txt file
.syn corpus + .synt template


Destinations
Internal results
IRaMuTeQ (via script), CSV, JSON, Excel, graphs


Interpretive annotation
Not supported
CODE, CHAIN, MEMO, SCALE


Team work
Manual
Template as contract


Programmatic access
Not available
Python API



IRaMuTeQ remains the right tool for DHC, similarity and correspondence analysis. Synesis does not replace these analyses: it governs the corpus that feeds them and opens it to others.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
This Skill teaches Claude to run a Synesis project with you. It installs the tools, talks through your study, writes the template, runs the coding, checks every quotation against your sources and builds an audit dashboard that opens on your own computer.
The division of roles is the same as everywhere in Synesis: the AI proposes, the compiler checks, the researcher decides. Claude leads the conversation and prepares the files. Your research questions, your categories and the approval of the template stay yours.
The video is narrated in Portuguese (episode E06 of the Synesis 101 course).

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
What you need

Claude Desktop (Windows or macOS), on an account with access to the Code tab.
A folder on your computer for the project, and your sources. No need to organize them first: the Skill shows where to put them and in which format (see Add your sources).
An internet connection the first time, to install the tools.
About an hour for the first session.

You do not need to install Python or know how to program. VS Code is optional.






Code tab only



The Skill needs a terminal and your disk. It works in the Code tab of Claude Desktop (a local session), and not in claude.ai chat or Cowork.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
1. Install the Skill (once)

Download the Skill file: synesis-skill.zip.
In Claude Desktop, open Customize → Plugins and use Add to upload the file.
Desktop warns you to install only plugins you trust. This is the Synesis project’s plugin.

If your organization does not allow uploading plugins, ask your administrator.






Already have an earlier version?



Remove the Synesis plugin in Customize → Plugins and upload the new file. Your projects do not change.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
2. Open the first session

Open the Code tab and choose the project folder.
Choose the Manual permission mode. Claude then asks for your approval before every command, so you see what will be installed.
Type /synesis and say what you want to do. For example:

/synesis I want to code my three interviews about telemedicine with Synesis. The transcripts are in the fontes folder.


If you just want to try it, use the example folder.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
3. What Claude does
In order:

Asks about confidentiality before opening any file (see Data confidentiality).
Installs the Synesis tools and shows a report. This happens once per computer.
Receives your sources: creates a folder, says what each file is and recommends a format. You decide.
Talks through the study: your research questions, what to extract from the sources, whether you want free or closed categories, causal relations or scales.
Writes the template (the description of what will be coded) and shows an example. You approve the template.
Codes each source, one at a time, and builds the ontology of concepts.
Validates, checks each quotation against the original text and builds the dashboard.

Throughout the work you follow the project in a page that opens in your browser: the project view.
At the end Claude summarizes the result: compiler errors and warnings, how many quotations were found in the sources, how many concepts the ontology has, and a list of points worth checking in your audit.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
Add your sources
In the first session Claude creates the inbox/ folder and opens the Your sources page. Copy your files there, as they are, and tell Claude.



The Your sources page


A program looks at the files on your computer and says what to do with each one. Your originals are never changed.








What you have
Format
What is coded




articles, in a literature review
.bib with abstracts (Zotero, Mendeley, Scopus, Web of Science)
only the abstract of each reference


interviews, field notes, documents, full articles
.txt, .md or .docx
the whole text


forms, open answers, posts, news, curricula
.toml, one record per file
the sections the template points to









PDF



Convert PDF files to .txt (UTF-8) before adding them. The page shows how, and what to check: columns, headers, broken words, scanned pages. With no confidential data, a PDF connector for Claude can help; ask Claude.








Personal data



Before copying interviews, remove names and other data that identify people, in the text and in the file names. You can also ask Claude for neutral keys (ent01, ent02…).

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
section: Follow the work: the project view
text:
Follow the work: the project view
The Skill keeps the page view/index.html, which opens with a double click, with no internet. It is read-only and updates at every step. Open the project view of the example.



The Overview of the project view



Overview: the research questions, the size of the corpus, what needs attention and the concepts-by-source matrix. Click a cell to read the excerpts.
Where to start: the next steps of your project.
The files: every block is a card, with its origin and its problems in plain words. Hover over the words in blue to understand the language.
Ask Claude: copies a ready request about that block, for you to paste in the conversation. Claude explains and proposes, and waits for your approval.
Possibilities: starts from what you want to investigate (compare, connect, organize, support an interpretation) and shows the Synesis feature that does it.

The page speaks the language of your project: English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, German, Italian or Chinese.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
What the Skill produces
The examples below come from a real session with the three fictitious interviews in the example folder. They are ordinary Synesis text files; you can open them in any editor.
The example project is in Portuguese, so its field names and concepts are too.




Project (telemedicina.synp)


The project gathers the files and records the research questions.
PROJECT telemedicina_rural
TEMPLATE "template.synt"
INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "referencias.bib"
INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "anotacoes"
INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontologia"

QUESTIONS
    Q1: Que barreiras ao uso da telemedicina os entrevistados relatam?
    Q2: Que benefícios da telemedicina os entrevistados percebem?
    Q3: Que relações causais entre fatores os entrevistados afirmam?
END QUESTIONS
...
END PROJECT






Template (template.synt)


Every field has instructions (GUIDELINES) with examples from another topic, so the model does not copy from your sources.
FIELD trecho TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Trecho copiado literalmente da fala do entrevistado
    GUIDELINES
        Copie de uma a três frases contínuas, exatamente como aparecem na fonte.
        Copie apenas falas do entrevistado, nunca as perguntas do entrevistador.
        Não corrija, não resuma, não junte frases distantes.
        Correto: "Depois que pintaram a faixa, comecei a ir de bicicleta todo dia."
        Errado: "A moradora passou a usar a bicicleta diariamente após a faixa."
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD






Annotations (anotacoes/)


Each excerpt becomes an ITEM: the literal quotation, the note, the codes and, when the source states it, a chain.
SOURCE @entrevista_dona_maria
    descricao: Entrevista fictícia com agricultora de 62 anos, moradora de comunidade rural, sobre o uso de consulta por vídeo.
END SOURCE

ITEM @entrevista_dona_maria
    trecho: O doutor não me tocou, não olhou a minha perna de perto. Para mim, médico bom é aquele que põe a mão na gente. Se não pode examinar, eu fico achando que ele não viu direito.
    nota: A fonte afirma que a ausência de toque e exame físico gera desconfiança sobre a qualidade do atendimento; sugere barreira de natureza cultural e de confiança, distinta da técnica.
    codigos: exame_fisico, confianca_no_atendimento
    cadeia: exame_fisico -> HABILITA -> confianca_no_atendimento
END ITEM






Ontology (ontologia/)


Each concept gets a definition with a criterion for applying it, and a theme.
ONTOLOGY exame_fisico
    definicao: Avaliação clínica direta do corpo do paciente por meio de toque, inspeção e palpação durante o atendimento, percebida pelos entrevistados como sinal de que o médico examinou de fato. Aplica-se quando a fonte menciona a presença, a ausência ou a necessidade desse contato físico no atendimento; não se aplica a conversa ou observação apenas por vídeo sem referência ao exame.
    grupo: pratica_clinica
END ONTOLOGY

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
4. Audit the result
The dashboard is in dashboard/dashboard.html. It opens with a double click, with no internet and no server.







Tab
What it shows




Fontes (Sources)
each coded excerpt, with its quotation, note and codes. The quotation appears as found, not found or unverifiable in the original text


Códigos (Codes)
each code, with its definition and all its evidence


Relações and Questões (Relations, Questions)
the relations between concepts and where the evidence for each research question is


Qualidade (Quality)
what still needs attention


Método (Method)
the full template and how the result was produced



To record your audit:

Mark excerpts and codes as correct, incorrect or doubt, with a note.
Use Exportar marcações (export marks) and hand the file to Claude in the conversation, so it records it in the project. Marks you do not export stay only in the browser and can be lost.

When something is wrong, Claude does not fix the excerpt by hand. It classifies the problem with you first: an ambiguous instruction in the template, a one-off failure, a badly converted source text, or a legitimate difference of interpretation.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
Try the example
Want to see the Skill at work without using your own sources? Download the example folder. It holds:

fontes/: three fictitious interviews about telemedicine in rural communities, ready for the Skill to code. Copy the folder somewhere new, open it in the Code tab and type:

/synesis I want to code my three interviews about telemedicine. The transcripts are in fontes.

resultado/: what the Skill produced in a real session with those interviews, so you can compare with yours: project, template, annotations, ontology and the dashboard. To see the dashboard right now, open the example dashboard or the project view.







Note



The coding is done by an AI model. Your result will be similar to the one in resultado/, not identical: compare structure and criteria, not every word.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
Costs
There are two coding modes, and Claude explains both before starting:








Mode
Who codes
Cost




Claude session
the Claude of your own subscription
within the limits of your plan


API
a model through an API key (Anthropic, OpenRouter)
billed by the provider; Claude runs a pilot with 2 or 3 sources and shows the cost before coding everything









API keys



Never type an API key into the chat. Claude creates a .env file in the project folder with the field empty, and you paste the key directly into it.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
Data confidentiality
Everything Claude reads leaves your computer and goes to Anthropic (and, in API mode, to the chosen provider). That is why Claude asks before opening your sources and proposes a modality:

A. Cloud: Claude reads the sources. Use it when there is no confidential data.
B. Reduced exposure: Claude works only with the method and invented examples; coding runs on a local model (Ollama). This is not fully local processing.
C. Local: Claude does not take part. For data under strict legal or ethical confidentiality, use Synesis in VS Code with a local model.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
section: What stays in the project folder
text:
What stays in the project folder







File or folder
Content




*.synp
the project


template.synt
the method


*.bib
the bibliographic sources


inbox/
your original files; do not share it if it has personal data


fontes/
the prepared texts


anotacoes/, ontologia/

runs/
the record of every run: what was asked of the model, what it answered and the decisions you made


view/, dashboard/, saida/
generated files, which can be rebuilt at any time



Keep the whole folder; when you share it, leave out the .env and the inbox/. With it, anyone can rebuild your results and your dashboard. The files are plain Synesis files: you can open them in VS Code whenever you like.

title: Synesis in Claude Desktop
text:
If something goes wrong

“command not found” right after installation: open a new session in the Code tab. In the same session, Claude uses the full path to the tools.
Windows blocked the installer: Claude tries another route. On an institutional machine you may need to talk to IT support.
Questions about the language: ask Claude, which consults the installed reference guide.
Synesis errors and suggestions: open an issue at https://github.com/synesis-lang/synesis/issues.

title: Getting Started with Synesis
text:
In this tutorial we will build your first complete Synesis project together. By the end you will have created a system of structured annotations, validated its consistency and exported the results for analysis.
What you will build:

A project analysing interviews about technology adoption
A custom template defining fields and rules
Structured interpretive annotations
An ontology of conceptual codes
Exports to JSON, CSV and Excel

Prerequisites:

Python 3.10 or later installed
VS Code (recommended, but optional)
30 minutes of dedicated time







Prefer to start by talking?



The Synesis Skill for Claude Desktop installs the tools and builds the project with you. This tutorial walks the same path by hand, so that you understand each piece.





Open a terminal and run:
pip install synesis
Check it:
synesis --version
The output starts like this:
synesis 0.16.0






Checkpoint ✓



If you see the version number, the compiler is installed. If not, see Troubleshooting.


For real-time validation in the editor, also install the language server, VS Code and the Synesis extension:
pip install synesis-lsp
The instructions are in the Synesis Explorer Tutorial.




Create a folder and initialize the project:
mkdir my-first-project
cd my-first-project
synesis init
What happened? Synesis created five files:
my-first-project/
├── project.synp       # project file (orchestrator)
├── template.synt      # template (defines the fields)
├── references.bib     # bibliography
├── annotations.syn    # annotations
└── ontology.syno      # ontology
The new project is a small example that already compiles:
synesis compile project.synp
In the next steps we replace the content of these files with our own study.




The template is the contract between you and the compiler. Open template.synt in your editor (code template.synt, or a plain text editor) and replace the whole content with:

TEMPLATE analysis version: "1.0"

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote, memo, code
    OPTIONAL chain
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Literal quotation taken from the source
    GUIDELINES
        Copy one to three sentences exactly as they appear in the source.
        Do not correct or summarize.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD memo TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Your interpretation of the excerpt
    GUIDELINES
        Explain in one or two sentences what the excerpt reveals.
        Do not repeat the quotation.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD code TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Ontology concepts the excerpt is evidence of
    GUIDELINES
        Use only concepts defined in the ontology.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    DESCRIPTION Causal relation between concepts, when the excerpt states it
    RELATIONS
        INHIBITS: one factor reduces or prevents another
        FAVORS: one factor promotes or eases another
    END RELATIONS
    GUIDELINES
        Record the relation only when the source states it.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED definition, group
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Definition of the concept and when to apply it
    GUIDELINES
        Define it in one or two sentences, with the application criterion.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD group TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Theme that groups the concept
    GUIDELINES
        Use a single term, without spaces.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD
What does this mean?

ITEM FIELDS and ONTOLOGY FIELDS say which fields each block accepts and which are required
Each FIELD declares the type and the scope of a field
ARITY >= 2 requires a chain to link at least two concepts
RELATIONS fixes the allowed relations
GUIDELINES records how to fill in the field: it is your coding protocol, for people and for AI







Golden Rule



The template is the single source of truth. What you declare here, the compiler validates. What you use without declaring, it refuses. The field names are yours.


Check the template:
synesis validate-template template.synt




Replace the content of ontology.syno with:

ONTOLOGY cost
    definition: Economic factors linked to price and required investment
    group: adoption_factors
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY ease_of_use
    definition: Perceived simplicity or complexity of the technology
    group: adoption_factors
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY perceived_usefulness
    definition: Belief that the technology will bring practical benefits
    group: adoption_factors
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY ai_adoption
    definition: Decision to bring artificial intelligence into the organization's processes
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY




Replace the content of references.bib with:

@misc{interview_john2026,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {Interview on AI adoption},
  year = {2026},
  note = {IT manager, mid-sized company (fictitious data)}
}

@misc{interview_mary2026,
  author = {Jones, Mary},
  title = {Interview on technology resistance},
  year = {2026},
  note = {Systems analyst, startup (fictitious data)}
}






Real interviews



Do not record participants’ names. Use neutral keys (int01, int02) and remove identifying data from the texts.






Now the main part. Replace the content of annotations.syn with:

SOURCE @interview_john2026
END SOURCE

ITEM @interview_john2026
    quote: "The upfront cost is prohibitive for our scale of operation"
    memo: The interviewee presents an economic barrier to AI adoption
    code: cost, ai_adoption
    chain: cost -> INHIBITS -> ai_adoption
END ITEM

ITEM @interview_john2026
    quote: "It looks very complex, we have nobody who knows how to do it"
    memo: The lack of technical skills appears as an obstacle
    code: ease_of_use
END ITEM

SOURCE @interview_mary2026
END SOURCE

ITEM @interview_mary2026
    quote: "If it were cheaper, we would try it. The technology looks good"
    memo: Acknowledges usefulness, but cost limits the decision
    code: cost, perceived_usefulness
    chain: cost -> INHIBITS -> ai_adoption
    chain: perceived_usefulness -> FAVORS -> ai_adoption
END ITEM






Notice the pattern



Each ITEM links:

a literal quotation (quote)
your interpretation (memo)
concepts (code)
when the source states it, a relation (chain)

This is bidirectional traceability: from evidence to interpretation and back.






To check only the syntax of a file:
synesis check annotations.syn
To validate the whole project (template, bibliography, annotations and ontology):
synesis compile project.synp --stats
The output ends like this:
Compilation Summary:
  Sources        2
  Items          3
  Model entries  4  (4 concepts)
  Active codes   4
  Chains         3






Checkpoint ✓



No line with [ERROR] or [WARNING]: the project is consistent.




Append to annotations.syn an item with a code that does not exist and an undeclared relation:

ITEM @interview_mary2026
    quote: "We would need training"
    memo: Points to the need for training
    code: training
    chain: training -> REQUIRES -> ai_adoption
END ITEM
synesis compile project.synp --check-codes
The compiler points to the file, the line and the problem: the relation REQUIRES is an error, and the code training, which has no concept in the ontology, a warning. Remove the item before going on.





synesis compile project.synp --json out/analysis.json --csv out/csv --xls out/analysis.xlsx
What was generated:
out/
├── analysis.json       # full project structure
├── analysis.xlsx       # workbook with several sheets
└── csv/
    ├── items.csv       # one row per analytical unit
    ├── ontologies.csv  # concepts
    └── chains.csv      # relations (from, relation, to)
There is a sources.csv when the template declares SOURCE fields.






Explore the results



Open analysis.xlsx in Excel or LibreOffice: you can already count, filter and cross your qualitative data, and every row points to its source file and line.




To avoid repeating the options, declare the artifacts in project.synp:

PROJECT technology_adoption
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"

    QUESTIONS
        Q1: Which factors do interviewees point to for adopting AI or not?
    END QUESTIONS

    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/analysis.json"
    END EXPORT

    EXPORT XLS
        OUTPUT "out/analysis.xlsx"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
And run:
synesis export project.synp





With the Synesis extension installed, open the project folder:
code .
You get syntax highlighting, real-time validation, autocompletion of codes and relations, and the views of references, codes, relations and ontology. See the Synesis Explorer Tutorial.




You created your first complete Synesis project. You learned to:

✅ Install the compiler and create a project
✅ Define your own template
✅ Create an ontology
✅ Register sources and write structured annotations
✅ Validate and read diagnostics
✅ Export to JSON, CSV and Excel








Guide for Researchers
Language Reference





How to define an ontology
How to create chains
AI coding (synesis-coder)
How to export to Neo4j





Why not Excel?
Why structured annotation matters








The Python scripts folder is not on the PATH.
python -m pip install --user synesis
Open a new terminal after installing. Alternatively, install with uv tool install synesis.



Either the path is wrong (run the commands in the project folder) or the template has a syntax error: the message can be the same in both cases. Check with:
synesis validate-template template.synt
The most common causes are version: on its own line, an ORDERED index without brackets and a missing END.



You used a code with no block in ontology.syno. Add the corresponding ONTOLOGY or fix the spelling.



The key does not exist in references.bib, or is spelled differently.



They are all in the Error Guide. In the terminal: pip install synesis-help and synesis-help lookup E010.

Questions? Open a discussion on GitHub Discussions or read the documentation.

ITEM @interview_mary2026
    quote: "We would need training"
    memo: Points to the need for training
    code: training
    chain: training -> REQUIRES -> ai_adoption
END ITEM
synesis compile project.synp --check-codes
The compiler points to the file, the line and the problem: the relation REQUIRES is an error, and the code training, which has no concept in the ontology, a warning. Remove the item before going on.

title: Getting Started with Synesis
text:
synesis compile project.synp --json out/analysis.json --csv out/csv --xls out/analysis.xlsx
What was generated:
out/
├── analysis.json       # full project structure
├── analysis.xlsx       # workbook with several sheets
└── csv/
    ├── items.csv       # one row per analytical unit
    ├── ontologies.csv  # concepts
    └── chains.csv      # relations (from, relation, to)
There is a sources.csv when the template declares SOURCE fields.






Explore the results



Open analysis.xlsx in Excel or LibreOffice: you can already count, filter and cross your qualitative data, and every row points to its source file and line.




To avoid repeating the options, declare the artifacts in project.synp:

PROJECT technology_adoption
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "references.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "annotations.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "ontology.syno"

    QUESTIONS
        Q1: Which factors do interviewees point to for adopting AI or not?
    END QUESTIONS

    EXPORT JSON
        OUTPUT "out/analysis.json"
    END EXPORT

    EXPORT XLS
        OUTPUT "out/analysis.xlsx"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
And run:
synesis export project.synp

title: Getting Started with Synesis
text:
With the Synesis extension installed, open the project folder:
code .
You get syntax highlighting, real-time validation, autocompletion of codes and relations, and the views of references, codes, relations and ontology. See the Synesis Explorer Tutorial.

title: Getting Started with Synesis
text:
You created your first complete Synesis project. You learned to:

✅ Install the compiler and create a project
✅ Define your own template
✅ Create an ontology
✅ Register sources and write structured annotations

✅ Export to JSON, CSV and Excel
