        OUTPUT "out/t.jsonl"
    END EXPORT
END PROJECT
project.synp:6:5  [INFO]  EXPORT ALPACA training: built-in pairs drop `status` (qualifies `chain`); declare MAP ... TO OUTPUT
How to fix: Declare MAP ... TO OUTPUT including the qualifier.

title: The Organizing Model
text:
The ONTOLOGY blocks of a Synesis project are its organizing principles: the conceptual system through which the coded occurrences will be understood. The compiler calls them together the organizing model, and each block a model entry.
The name “ONTOLOGY” does not commit you to a formal ontology. The same mechanism serves several degrees of organization, and the degree is a research decision, not a format constraint:








Degree
What the project declares
What it is for




Flat list
a name and a definition per concept
controlled vocabulary: support_network and SupportNetwork do not become two concepts


Vocabulary with synonyms / thesaurus
alternative and hidden labels, deprecated names
search and consolidation of variants


Taxonomy
“is a kind of” hierarchy
counts per subtree, navigation from general to specific


Multi-relation taxonomy
hierarchy with more than one species (kind, part, instance) and associative relations
SKOS publication, integration with other vocabularies



No degree is called “ontology”: SKOS is a knowledge organization system (KOS) — vocabulary, thesaurus, taxonomy —, not a formal OWL ontology. The term is reserved for an OWL export.
None of this needs special syntax in the .syno: these are ordinary template fields (SCOPE ONTOLOGY) given a function with a ROLE line.


At the end of synesis compile, the compiler describes what the project declared — without judging whether the relations are valid:
Structural Profile:
  Concepts:              19
  With definition:       19 (100%)
  Alternative labels:    8
  With KIND parent:      7
  With PART parent:      2
  Cycles:                none ✓
  Organizing model:      Terminological: With synonyms (1 code without concept)  |  Conceptual: Multi-relation taxonomy
  EXPORT SKOS:           Terminological: Thesaurus  |  Conceptual: Multi-relation taxonomy
The Organizing model line profiles the .syno; each EXPORT SKOS block gets its own line, because an artifact may add relations (see MAP RELATIONS). All ecosystem CLIs write their output in English.



A field’s type gives the shape of its value; its ROLE line gives its function in the organizing model. The field name stays free.
FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
END FIELD

FIELD used_for TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE LABEL ALTERNATIVE
END FIELD

FIELD kind_of TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY KIND
END FIELD









Role
Type
Meaning
SKOS




LABEL PREFERRED
TEXT
display label (one per concept)
skos:prefLabel


LABEL ALTERNATIVE
TEXT
synonyms and variants
skos:altLabel


LABEL HIDDEN
TEXT
old or misspelled forms, for search only
skos:hiddenLabel


NOTE DEFINITION
TEXT
the concept’s definition
skos:definition


NOTE USAGE
TEXT
when to apply the code
skos:scopeNote


NOTE EXAMPLE
TEXT
typical case
skos:example


NOTE COUNTEREXAMPLE
TEXT
similar case it does not apply to
syn:counterExample


HIERARCHY KIND
CODE
is a kind of
skos:broader


HIERARCHY PART
CODE
is part of
skos:broader


HIERARCHY INSTANCE
CODE
is an instance of
skos:broader


USE
CODE
deprecated name; use the concept given
label of the target



With the function declared, the compiler validates the structure: a label belongs to one concept only, the hierarchy points to the broader concept, allows several parents and has no cycle. Each tool reads the field by its role: the SKOS exporter, the synesis-coder phases, synesis-graph (KIND_OF, PART_OF, INSTANCE_OF edges) and the LSP (hover with parents and children).
ONTOLOGY smishing
    definition: Phishing carried out through SMS messages.
    used_for: SMS phishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY


The hierarchy in the .syno is what the project adopts. What the sources state stays in the annotations’ chains (CHAIN), with evidence. The two do not mix: a chain smishing -> KIND_OF -> phishing puts nothing in the .syno. To bring it into an artifact, use MAP RELATIONS in the EXPORT block.



When two blocks name the same concept, the deprecated one keeps only the USE-role field:
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY
Annotations do not change. Counts, hierarchy, graph and SKOS add the deprecated block to its target, and the deprecated name becomes a label of the target. synesis-coder consolidate project.synp voice_phishing --into vishing makes the edit with a manifest; --revert undoes it.




The .synp can declare what the project must be able to answer:
QUESTIONS
    Q1: Which evidence concerns phishing or any of its subtypes?
    Q2: Which concepts have no direct or indirect evidence?
END QUESTIONS
The questions guide the template design and serve as acceptance criteria for the organizing model. They appear in the compiled JSON, in the graph context and in the project context synesis-coder sends to the model.



PHASE blocks split the production of the organizing model into phases, each with its own fields:
PHASE ONTOLOGY definitions
    FIELDS definition, topic
    INPUT excerpt, chain
END PHASE

PHASE ONTOLOGY synonyms
    FIELDS used_for, hidden_label
    INPUT definition, topic
END PHASE

PHASE ONTOLOGY taxonomy
    FIELDS kind_of, part_of
    INPUT definition, topic, chain
END PHASE
The compiler validates the plan against the template (existing fields, phase order, required fields covered). Each phase’s kind comes from the roles: HIERARCHY fields make a taxonomy phase, LABEL ALTERNATIVE or HIDDEN fields a synonyms phase, and the rest a descriptive phase.
synesis-coder phase project.synp --list          # the plan and each phase's connection
synesis-coder phase project.synp definitions     # run one phase
synesis-coder review project.synp taxonomy --sample 100
synesis-coder review project.synp taxonomy --score sample.csv
Each run writes a manifest (<destination>.<phase>.manifest.json) recording what was proposed, applied or rejected; running again with unchanged inputs does not call the model. review draws a stratified sample for human judgement and estimates precision with inclusion weights. Model and connection can differ per phase (SYNESIS_CODER_PHASE_<NAME>_MODEL, _BACKEND, _API_URL, _API_KEY).



A project’s artifacts are declared in EXPORT blocks of the .synp and run with synesis export project.synp. The SKOS format publishes the organizing model as a SKOS vocabulary (a KOS) in Turtle:
EXPORT SKOS corroborated
    OUTPUT "out/fraud.ttl"
    NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/fraud/"
    LANGUAGE en
    MIN_SOURCES 2
    MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO HIERARCHY KIND
    MAP RELATIONS MITIGATES, EXPLOITS TO RELATED
END EXPORT

MAP RELATIONS brings chain relations into a role (HIERARCHY KIND, PART, INSTANCE or RELATED) in this artifact only. The .syno, dashboards and graph do not see the mapping.
MIN_SOURCES is the minimum number of distinct sources stating a pair for it to enter the file. Two blocks with different thresholds separate the corroborated pairs from the candidates.
ALIAS_LABEL HIDDEN|ALTERNATIVE decides how a deprecated name (USE) enters its target; the default is HIDDEN.
REGISTRY "<file>" with synesis export --publish records the published IRIs. If a published concept is later deprecated, its old IRI is exported as obsolete (owl:deprecated, dcterms:isReplacedBy) instead of disappearing.



Each concept gets the IRI NAMESPACE + concept/ + block name. The NAMESPACE belongs to the project: a domain the team controls and keeps, ending in / or #. example.org is for testing, never for publication. Because the IRI derives from the name, renaming a concept changes its IRI: after publishing, use USE with REGISTRY so the old IRI keeps resolving to the new one.
The NAMESPACE is the researcher’s decision: changing it blocks neither the export nor the publication. If the REGISTRY holds IRIs from another namespace, synesis export warns how many were left out of the check (SYNESIS_E156) — links to them break unless the old address redirects. With --publish, an unreadable REGISTRY is an error (nothing is written), and OUTPUT and REGISTRY on the same file are always refused (SYNESIS_E157).



SKOS covers almost everything. The two missing terms are in the syn: vocabulary (https://synesis-lang.org/ns/syn#, file syn.ttl):

syn:counterExample, subproperty of skos:note, for NOTE COUNTEREXAMPLE;
syn:classifiedBy, superproperty of the properties generated for ENUMERATED and ORDERED fields, whose values become skos:ConceptScheme.

Synesis API

title: 1 Synesis: In-Memory API (synesis.load)
text:
Verified with synesis 0.16.0



The synesis.load API compiles Synesis projects directly in memory, with no files on disk. It suits:

Jupyter Notebooks: interactive analysis of qualitative data
Python scripts: automating research pipelines
Pandas integration: direct export to DataFrames
Testing and prototyping: quick validation of annotations






Aspect
CLI (synesis compile)
API (synesis.load)




Input
Files on disk
Strings in memory


Output
Files
Dicts, tables, DataFrames


Use
Terminal, CI/CD
Notebooks, scripts


I/O
Reads and writes disk
None



To compile a project that is on disk, use synesis.SynesisCompiler("project.synp").compile().





pip install synesis
pip install pandas        # optional, for the DataFrame methods
import synesis
print(synesis.__version__)  # e.g. 0.16.0










Strings start at column 0



Indentation is significant in Synesis. A string whose whole content is indented (common in Python code) is a syntax error: write the text at column 0 or use textwrap.dedent.


import synesis

template = """
TEMPLATE Minimal

SOURCE FIELDS
    OPTIONAL date
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD date TYPE DATE
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
"""

project = """
PROJECT Demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
END PROJECT
"""

annotations = {
    "sample.syn": """
SOURCE @ref2024
    date: 2024-06-15
END SOURCE

ITEM @ref2024
    quote: The technology shows promising results.
END ITEM
"""
}

bibliography = """
@article{ref2024,
    author = {Silva, Maria},
    title = {A Study on Technology},
    year = {2024}
}
"""

result = synesis.load(
    project_content=project,
    template_content=template,
    annotation_contents=annotations,
    bibliography_content=bibliography,
)

if result.success:
    print(f"Compiled: {result.stats.item_count} item(s)")
    print(result.to_dataframe("items"))
else:
    print(result.get_diagnostics())






def load(
    project_content: str,
    template_content: str,
    annotation_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    ontology_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    bibliography_content: Optional[str] = None,
    dataset_index: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    project_filename: str = "<project>",
    template_filename: str = "<template>",
    bibliography_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    check_codes: bool = False,
) -> MemoryCompilationResult












Parameter
Type
Required
Description




project_content
str
Yes
Content of the .synp


template_content
str
Yes
Content of the .synt


annotation_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
{name: content} of the .syn files


ontology_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
{name: content} of the .syno files


bibliography_content
str
No
Content of one .bib


bibliography_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
Several .bib files, merged in dictionary order (do not combine with the previous one)


dataset_index
Dict
No
Pre-loaded TOML records, for ON DATASET fields


check_codes
bool
No
True: one warning per occurrence of a code without a concept (E004); False: one summary (E090)


project_filename
str
No
Virtual name used in error messages


template_filename
str
No
Virtual name used in error messages



The function does not read the disk: the INCLUDE lines of the project are not followed; only what you pass goes in.



import synesis

project = """
PROJECT QualitativeResearch
    TEMPLATE "analysis.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "refs.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "interviews.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "concepts.syno"
END PROJECT
"""

template = """
TEMPLATE QualitativeAnalysis

SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED date
    OPTIONAL country
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    REQUIRED BUNDLE note, chain
    OPTIONAL code
END ITEM FIELDS

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED description
    OPTIONAL topic
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD date TYPE DATE
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD country TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD code TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        INFLUENCES: Relation of influence
        ENABLES: Enabling relation
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD

FIELD description TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
END FIELD

FIELD topic TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
END FIELD
"""

annotations = """
SOURCE @silva2024
    date: 2024-03-15
    country: Brazil
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: Cost is a significant barrier.
    note: The interviewee identifies an economic factor
    chain: Cost -> INFLUENCES -> Adoption
END ITEM

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: Public acceptance eases implementation.
    note: Relation between social and technical factors
    chain: Public_Acceptance -> ENABLES -> Implementation
END ITEM
"""

concepts = """
ONTOLOGY Cost
    description: Economic cost factor
    topic: Economics
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Public_Acceptance
    description: Community acceptance
    topic: Social_Factors
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Adoption
    description: Technology adoption
    topic: Technology
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Implementation
    description: Technical implementation
    topic: Technology
END ONTOLOGY
"""

title: 1 Synesis: In-Memory API (synesis.load)
text:
The synesis.load API compiles Synesis projects directly in memory, with no files on disk. It suits:

Jupyter Notebooks: interactive analysis of qualitative data
Python scripts: automating research pipelines
Pandas integration: direct export to DataFrames
Testing and prototyping: quick validation of annotations






Aspect
CLI (synesis compile)
API (synesis.load)




Input
Files on disk
Strings in memory


Output
Files
Dicts, tables, DataFrames


Use
Terminal, CI/CD
Notebooks, scripts


I/O
Reads and writes disk
None



To compile a project that is on disk, use synesis.SynesisCompiler("project.synp").compile().

title: 1 Synesis: In-Memory API (synesis.load)
text:
Strings start at column 0



Indentation is significant in Synesis. A string whose whole content is indented (common in Python code) is a syntax error: write the text at column 0 or use textwrap.dedent.


import synesis

template = """
TEMPLATE Minimal

SOURCE FIELDS
    OPTIONAL date
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD date TYPE DATE
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD
"""

project = """
PROJECT Demo
    TEMPLATE "template.synt"
END PROJECT
"""

annotations = {
    "sample.syn": """
SOURCE @ref2024
    date: 2024-06-15
END SOURCE

ITEM @ref2024
    quote: The technology shows promising results.
END ITEM
"""
}

bibliography = """
@article{ref2024,
    author = {Silva, Maria},
    title = {A Study on Technology},
    year = {2024}
}
"""

result = synesis.load(
    project_content=project,
    template_content=template,
    annotation_contents=annotations,
    bibliography_content=bibliography,
)

if result.success:
    print(f"Compiled: {result.stats.item_count} item(s)")
    print(result.to_dataframe("items"))
else:
    print(result.get_diagnostics())

def load(
    project_content: str,
    template_content: str,
    annotation_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    ontology_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    bibliography_content: Optional[str] = None,
    dataset_index: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    project_filename: str = "<project>",
    template_filename: str = "<template>",
    bibliography_contents: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    check_codes: bool = False,
) -> MemoryCompilationResult












Parameter
Type
Required
Description




project_content
str
Yes
Content of the .synp


template_content
str
Yes
Content of the .synt


annotation_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
{name: content} of the .syn files


ontology_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
{name: content} of the .syno files


bibliography_content
str
No
Content of one .bib


bibliography_contents
Dict[str, str]
No
Several .bib files, merged in dictionary order (do not combine with the previous one)


dataset_index
Dict
No
Pre-loaded TOML records, for ON DATASET fields


check_codes
bool
No
True: one warning per occurrence of a code without a concept (E004); False: one summary (E090)


project_filename
str
No
Virtual name used in error messages


template_filename
str
No
Virtual name used in error messages



The function does not read the disk: the INCLUDE lines of the project are not followed; only what you pass goes in.



import synesis

project = """
PROJECT QualitativeResearch
    TEMPLATE "analysis.synt"
    INCLUDE BIBLIOGRAPHY "refs.bib"
    INCLUDE ANNOTATIONS "interviews.syn"
    INCLUDE ONTOLOGY "concepts.syno"
END PROJECT
"""

template = """
TEMPLATE QualitativeAnalysis

SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED date
    OPTIONAL country
END SOURCE FIELDS

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote
    REQUIRED BUNDLE note, chain
    OPTIONAL code
END ITEM FIELDS

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED description
    OPTIONAL topic
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD date TYPE DATE
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD country TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE SOURCE
END FIELD

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD note TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD code TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ITEM
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    RELATIONS
        INFLUENCES: Relation of influence
        ENABLES: Enabling relation
    END RELATIONS
END FIELD

FIELD description TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
END FIELD

FIELD topic TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
END FIELD
"""

annotations = """
SOURCE @silva2024
    date: 2024-03-15
    country: Brazil
END SOURCE

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: Cost is a significant barrier.
    note: The interviewee identifies an economic factor
    chain: Cost -> INFLUENCES -> Adoption
END ITEM

ITEM @silva2024
    quote: Public acceptance eases implementation.
    note: Relation between social and technical factors
    chain: Public_Acceptance -> ENABLES -> Implementation
END ITEM
"""

concepts = """
ONTOLOGY Cost
    description: Economic cost factor
    topic: Economics
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Public_Acceptance
    description: Community acceptance
    topic: Social_Factors
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Adoption
    description: Technology adoption
    topic: Technology
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY Implementation
    description: Technical implementation
    topic: Technology
END ONTOLOGY
"""

bibliography = """
@article{silva2024,
    author = {Silva, João and Santos, Maria},
    title = {Factors of Technology Adoption},
    journal = {Brazilian Research Journal},
    year = {2024}
}
"""

result = synesis.load(
    project_content=project,
    template_content=template,
    annotation_contents={"interviews.syn": annotations},
    ontology_contents={"concepts.syno": concepts},
    bibliography_content=bibliography,
)

if result.success:
    print(f"Sources: {result.stats.source_count}")
    print(f"Items: {result.stats.item_count}")
    print(f"Ontologies: {result.stats.ontology_count}")
    print(f"Chains: {result.stats.chain_count}")

Items: 2
Ontologies: 4
Chains: 2

title: Synesis for Qualitative Research
text:
In this tutorial we will build a qualitative analysis project together using Synesis. If you work with interviews, document analysis, grounded theory or thematic analysis, this guide is for you.
What you will build:

An interview analysis project
A conceptual coding system
Causal relations between concepts
Exports for quantitative analysis

Prerequisites:

Python 3.10+ and the compiler installed (pip install synesis)
A reference manager (Zotero recommended, but optional)
Basic familiarity with qualitative research







New to Synesis?



If you have never used Synesis, start with Getting Started. This tutorial assumes you know the basic commands.





We will work on a fictitious study about resistance to telemedicine adoption in rural communities. Imagine you ran 3 semi-structured interviews and now need to analyse the data.




Create a project folder:
mkdir telemedicine-analysis
cd telemedicine-analysis
Create references.bib with the references of the interviews. The keys are neutral and do not identify participants:

@misc{interview01,
  author = {Participant 01},
  title = {Interview on access to health care},
  year = {2026},
  note = {Resident of a rural community, 45 minutes (fictitious data)}
}

@misc{interview02,
  author = {Participant 02},
  title = {Interview on technology and health},
  year = {2026},
  note = {Resident of a rural community, 60 minutes (fictitious data)}
}

@misc{interview03,
  author = {Participant 03},
  title = {Interview, professional perspective},
  year = {2026},
  note = {Rural physician, 40 minutes (fictitious data)}
}






Checkpoint ✓



You should have the folder telemedicine-analysis/ with the file references.bib and your 3 interviews.






Create template.synt, fitted to qualitative analysis:

TEMPLATE qualitative_analysis version: "1.0"

# ============================================
# SOURCE FIELDS
# ============================================

SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED speaker
END SOURCE FIELDS

FIELD speaker TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Who speaks in the source
    VALUES
        User: Resident served by the service
        Professional: Health professional
    END VALUES
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ITEM FIELDS
# ============================================

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote, memo, chain
    OPTIONAL context
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Textual excerpt from the interview
    GUIDELINES
        Copy the speech literally, in one to three sentences.
        Do not copy the interviewer's questions.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD memo TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Analytical memo with the interpretation and the mechanism identified
    GUIDELINES
        Interpret the speech; do not repeat it.
        Separate what the source states from what you infer.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    DESCRIPTION Causal or relational chain between ontology concepts
    RELATIONS
        MEDIATES: one factor softens or mediates the effect of another
        FAVORS: direct positive effect (A favors B)
        INHIBITS: limits or restricts (A reduces the viability of B)
        ENABLES: creates a condition for B to happen
    END RELATIONS
    GUIDELINES
        Record only relations the speech supports.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD context TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Nuances of the moment of speech (tone, emotion, hesitation)
    GUIDELINES
        Fill in only with what was recorded during the interview.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ONTOLOGY
# ============================================

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED definition, group
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Definition of the concept and application criterion
    GUIDELINES
        Define the concept and say when to apply it.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD group TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Thematic group of the concept
    GUIDELINES
        Use a term without spaces.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD
Notice: the context field is optional and records qualitative nuances (hesitation, emotion, changes of tone).






Checkpoint ✓



Validate the template:
synesis validate-template template.synt
It should print OK.






In qualitative research codes emerge from the data; let us create the initial ones from a first reading. Create ontology.syno:

ONTOLOGY technological_distrust
    definition: Fear about the effectiveness of remote medical care, such as doubting a diagnosis without physical examination.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY lack_of_infrastructure
    definition: Missing or precarious internet, equipment or power that makes use unfeasible.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY preference_for_in_person_contact
    definition: Valuing face-to-face meetings, linking quality of care to physical presence.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY low_digital_literacy
    definition: Difficulty with digital technologies, creating dependence on outside help.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY urgent_need
    definition: Emergency or lack of an in-person alternative that drives acceptance.
    group: facilitators
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY community_support
    definition: Help from relatives, neighbours or health agents that mediates access.
    group: facilitators
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_adoption
    definition: Patient's willingness to use remote medical services.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY access_to_telemedicine
    definition: Concrete capacity to connect and use the remote service.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_use
    definition: Actual use of remote consultations, autonomous or mediated.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_acceptance
    definition: Receptiveness to telemedicine after experience or perceived need.

title: Synesis for Qualitative Research
text: We will work on a fictitious study about resistance to telemedicine adoption in rural communities. Imagine you ran 3 semi-structured interviews and now need to analyse the data.

title: Synesis for Qualitative Research
Synesis for Qualitative Research
text:
Create template.synt, fitted to qualitative analysis:

TEMPLATE qualitative_analysis version: "1.0"

# ============================================
# SOURCE FIELDS
# ============================================

SOURCE FIELDS
    REQUIRED speaker
END SOURCE FIELDS

FIELD speaker TYPE ENUMERATED
    SCOPE SOURCE
    DESCRIPTION Who speaks in the source
    VALUES
        User: Resident served by the service
        Professional: Health professional
    END VALUES
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ITEM FIELDS
# ============================================

ITEM FIELDS
    REQUIRED quote, memo, chain
    OPTIONAL context
END ITEM FIELDS

FIELD quote TYPE QUOTATION
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Textual excerpt from the interview
    GUIDELINES
        Copy the speech literally, in one to three sentences.
        Do not copy the interviewer's questions.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD memo TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Analytical memo with the interpretation and the mechanism identified
    GUIDELINES
        Interpret the speech; do not repeat it.
        Separate what the source states from what you infer.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD chain TYPE CHAIN
    SCOPE ITEM
    ARITY >= 2
    DESCRIPTION Causal or relational chain between ontology concepts
    RELATIONS
        MEDIATES: one factor softens or mediates the effect of another
        FAVORS: direct positive effect (A favors B)
        INHIBITS: limits or restricts (A reduces the viability of B)
        ENABLES: creates a condition for B to happen
    END RELATIONS
    GUIDELINES
        Record only relations the speech supports.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD context TYPE MEMO
    SCOPE ITEM
    DESCRIPTION Nuances of the moment of speech (tone, emotion, hesitation)
    GUIDELINES
        Fill in only with what was recorded during the interview.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

# ============================================
# ONTOLOGY
# ============================================

ONTOLOGY FIELDS
    REQUIRED definition, group
END ONTOLOGY FIELDS

FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Definition of the concept and application criterion
    GUIDELINES
        Define the concept and say when to apply it.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD

FIELD group TYPE TOPIC
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    DESCRIPTION Thematic group of the concept
    GUIDELINES
        Use a term without spaces.
    END GUIDELINES
END FIELD
Notice: the context field is optional and records qualitative nuances (hesitation, emotion, changes of tone).






Checkpoint ✓



Validate the template:
synesis validate-template template.synt
It should print OK.

title: Synesis for Qualitative Research
text:
In qualitative research codes emerge from the data; let us create the initial ones from a first reading. Create ontology.syno:

ONTOLOGY technological_distrust
    definition: Fear about the effectiveness of remote medical care, such as doubting a diagnosis without physical examination.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY lack_of_infrastructure
    definition: Missing or precarious internet, equipment or power that makes use unfeasible.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY preference_for_in_person_contact
    definition: Valuing face-to-face meetings, linking quality of care to physical presence.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY low_digital_literacy
    definition: Difficulty with digital technologies, creating dependence on outside help.
    group: barriers
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY urgent_need
    definition: Emergency or lack of an in-person alternative that drives acceptance.
    group: facilitators
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY community_support
    definition: Help from relatives, neighbours or health agents that mediates access.
    group: facilitators
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_adoption
    definition: Patient's willingness to use remote medical services.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY access_to_telemedicine
    definition: Concrete capacity to connect and use the remote service.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_use
    definition: Actual use of remote consultations, autonomous or mediated.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY telemedicine_acceptance
    definition: Receptiveness to telemedicine after experience or perceived need.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

ONTOLOGY in_depth_diagnosis
    definition: Diagnosis requiring physical examination, named as a context unsuited to telemedicine.
    group: outcomes
END ONTOLOGY

title: 1 Quick Guide: the Synesis Extension for VS Code
text:
Goal: help you install and use the Synesis extension (version 0.17) to write and navigate Synesis files (.synp, .synt, .syn, .syno, .synr). The extension is also known as Synesis Explorer.




Validates files as you type and completes fields, codes and relations
Shows references, codes, relations, ontology and template fields in side panels
Opens relation graphs and the abstracts of references
Codes a selected passage with synesis-coder
Chats with a graph database of the project in VS Code chat




VS Code start screen with the extension installed.







VS Code
Python 3.10 or later
The compiler and the language server, which do the analysis (the extension is the interface):

Search for Synesis (publisher synesis-lang)
Click Install

To install from a .vsix file, use the ... menu of the Extensions view and Install from VSIX….

text: Install synesis-coder (pip install synesis-coder), set the key in the project’s .env, select a passage in a .syn and run Synesis: Code Selection (Ctrl+Shift+I). See AI Coding.

title: 1 Quick Guide: the Synesis Extension for VS Code
text: The extension registers a chat participant that queries an ArcadeDB database of the project, created by synesis-graph. The commands Synesis: Settings (connections and providers), Synesis: Select Chat Graph Database and Synesis: Show Turn Evidence and Queries configure the chat and show the audit trail of each answer. Keys are kept in VS Code’s secure storage.

title: 1 Quick Guide: the Synesis Extension for VS Code
text:
In Settings, search for “Synesis” (prefix synesisExplorer.):







Setting
Purpose




lsp.pythonPath
path to the synesis-lsp executable, if not on PATH


lsp.enabled
turns the server on or off


diagnostics.enabled
shows the underlines


diagnostics.checkCodes
warns on every code missing from the ontology (off by default: one summary on the .synp)


inlayHints.enabled
shows “(Author, Year)” after references


semanticHighlighting.enabled
highlighting based on the syntax tree


completion.autoImportCodes
offers ontology codes on completion


coder.path
path to synesis-coder
